compareDisposition.rationale: No distinct two-source pairing adds more than this passage and its existing Scripture connections.

observations.body: Moses cuts tablets, makes an ark, ascends, receives the Ten Commandments written like the first, places them in the ark, and recalls Levi’s ministry and the command to journey.
observations.label: The second tablets are written and placed in the ark

observations.body: The second tablets are written and placed in the ark belongs to sinai remembered in the Sinai trail.
observations.label: Where this sits

observations.body: Deuteronomy 10:1–11 supplies later-memory evidence for the event’s developing sequence.
observations.label: Within the Sinai event

observations.body: Later witnesses select and reuse Sinai in their own settings; they remain later readings rather than replacements for the Exodus event.
observations.label: Reading boundary

payload.posture: Read Deuteronomy 10:1–11 as its own source before carrying it into the wider Sinai trail.
payload.tension: The second tablets are written and placed in the ark belongs to the sinai remembered movement, but its part in the event must remain distinct from the surrounding speech, response, breach, and renewal.
payload.title: The second tablets are written and placed in the ark
